On this map Poland has disappeared. Germany and the Soviet Union took just over five weeks to do it, and the split had been agreed in secret about a week before the first shot.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, dated 23 August 1939, was a non-aggression treaty with a secret protocol: eastern Poland, Latvia, Estonia, Finland and Bessarabia went to the Soviet sphere. The west only got proof of it at Nuremberg.
2/ Germany invaded on 1 September. Slovakia, a German client state since March, joined the attack. On 17 September the Red Army crossed from the east. The campaign ended on 6 October.

3/ Western Poland was annexed into the Reich and the east into the Soviet Union. The dark patch labelled General Government is the occupation zone Germany set up in the centre rather than annexing it outright.

4/ Around Poland the map had already moved that spring. Slovakia declared independence on 14 March, a day before Germany occupied Bohemia and Moravia. Italy invaded Albania on 7 April, and King Zog went into exile in Greece.
5/ The protocol wasn't finished. The Soviet Union invaded Finland on 30 November 1939, starting the Winter War, and was expelled from the League of Nations over the attack.
Could Poland have survived 1939 with different allies, or was the pact decisive? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
